title: Tech Note: 4D Plug-in Development Guide - Part 1
author: Keisuke Miyako, 4D Japan

historical_commentary.text: This is a foundational plug-in development guide written right as 4D v11 SQL introduced Unicode support, Universal Binary, and the retirement of QuickDraw and Altura-based Mac-to-Windows porting — a genuine technology inflection point for native 4D plug-ins. The core plug-in API and C/C++ toolchain approach (Xcode/Visual Studio) it describes remains largely valid today: 4D still supports compiled C-based plug-ins with a similar architecture, so this is still_relevant as an introduction to plug-in fundamentals. However, many of today's simpler cross-platform extension needs are now better served by 4D's project-based classes (introduced ~v18-19) or by calling external processes/REST APIs directly, reducing the need to write a full native plug-in for basic tasks.
related_updates: 4D language classes (introduced 4D v18/v19, ~2019-2020) for many extension needs that previously required a compiled plug-in
4D's modern native Unicode/UTF-8 text handling throughout the language, built on the foundations this note describes
Current 4D Plug-in API documentation reflects further API evolution since 4D v11
